requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Confirmed appworker did not exist beforehand (cmd-7d84f0b1929e4921), then created with useradd -m and id showed uid=1000(appworker) (cmd-d905432bcb114139). Post-restart getent passwd confirms it persisted (cmd-f0b2f1ba4115465b).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker's login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256 (cmd-b1af08a6510a4616), confirmed pam_limits wired into system-auth and verified via a real login shell (sudo -u appworker -i) that ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256 (cmd-c3bf1ff668af4271), reconfirmed identically after restart (cmd-f0b2f1ba4115465b).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id f54d7366... plus account/limits state (cmd-d2332159610d4720), matching the fixed before_prepare boot-identity snapshot. Reboot was triggered and acknowledged before disconnect (cmd-ed805e57d4124d42). Post-restart polling shows a timeout then success with new boot_id 4dcef926... (cmd-2f964946574c49de, cmd-fa5df62ff8e74c66), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot and the executor_comparison boot-identity diff. Post-restart verification shows appworker account and enforced ulimits (8192/256) intact (cmd-f0b2f1ba4115465b). Fixed snapshots also show no failed services and unchanged package health across the restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and constraining its login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes via pam_limits — are directly satisfied with pre- and post-restart verification. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, a differing post-restart boot identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and confirmed recovery of the account and its limits. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene concerns were identified.
limitations: The pam_limits enforcement was verified via 'sudo -u appworker -i' rather than an actual interactive SSH login session for appworker, which is a reasonable and commonly accepted proxy but not a fully independent login-session test.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so the preparation_comparison shows no changes by construction; this does not affect the executor-caused change analysis, which correctly uses after_prepare vs after_executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task outcomes or the restart protocol: account creation, limits file write, and the reboot sequence. The reboot leaves /tmp/reboot.log and new systemd-private ephemeral dirs, which are expected, low-risk byproducts of a native reboot rather than executor-introduced residue; no failed services, package inconsistency, or unsafe exposure appear in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found in the timeline.
